chunks: And it is narrated from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he said:

"There is no distressed person who comes to the Mosque of Al-Sahla, prays two rak'ahs in it between the two evening prayers, and supplicates Allah (the Exalted), except that Allah will relieve his distress."

key_terms.بَيْنَ الْعِشَاءَيْنِ: Between the two evening prayers (Maghrib and Isha)
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ السَّهْلَةِ: Mosque of Al-Sahla, a specific shrine in Kufa
key_terms.مَكْرُوبٍ: A person in distress or hardship

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying two rak'ahs at Masjid Al-Sahla when distressed?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the spiritual efficacy of Masjid Al-Sahla in Kufa as a locus for divine relief (*faraj*). It specifically prescribes performing two units of prayer between the evening prayers (*bayna al-'ishayn*), linking physical devotion in a sacred space with the alleviation of distress through supplication.
